subject: Sizing & Reserved Capacity for TritonHealth pilot — pricing guardrails
messages:
From: Anjali Rao <anjali@tritonhealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj.patel@tritonhealth.com>
Date: 2028-07-10T15:23:00-07:00
Subject: Sizing & Reserved Capacity for TritonHealth pilot — pricing guardrails

Marcus —

Thanks again for the demo earlier. TritonHealth is excited about the latency and cost profile you showed. Before we lock the pilot commitments with Procurement, we need Redwood to propose: 1) a recommended dedicated capacity sizing for our initial 12-month pilot (expected peak of 30k real-time inference calls/day, avg payload ~1.2k tokens), 2) a clear pricing/discount structure tied to reserved commit length and GPU-sku exposure, and 3) an outline for how Redwood will handle GPU-market price spikes (e.g., indexation, temporary credits, or fallback to shared pools).

Procurement is risk-averse — they want a guardrail so we can sign a reserved commitment without being heavily exposed if GPU spot/pricing shifts dramatically in months 3–6. Would you be able to send a short proposal (1–2 pages) and a phased activation schedule we can attach to the SOW by next Friday (7/19)?

Appreciate a pragmatic proposal rather than legalese.

—Anjali
VP Product, TritonHealth

--
Attachment: triton_usage_sample.csv (referenced for our internal projections)
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Anjali Rao <anjali@tritonhealth.com>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj.patel@tritonhealth.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-11T09:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sizing & Reserved Capacity for TritonHealth pilot — pricing guardrails

Anjali —

Thanks for the clear ask. High level: based on the numbers you shared (30k peak calls/day, ~1.2k avg tokens), our initial recommendation is a phased reserved pool equivalent to ~40 mGPU vGPUs (NVIDIA A100-equivalent slices) with burst capacity to 60 vGPUs for predictable spiky days. Phase plan (attached spreadsheet): immediate reserve of 20 vGPUs for months 1–3, +10 vGPUs month 4, +10 vGPUs month 7 as usage ramps.

Pricing guardrails we propose to protect both sides:
- 12-month reserved commitment with a baseline discount band of 18% off list for the committed tier.
- A GPU-indexation fallback: if our underlying GPU procurement cost moves >12% quarter-over-quarter we trigger a review and either (a) temporary credit applied to your invoice to offset increased unit costs for 60 days, or (b) automatic allowed burst to our hosted pool at the committed rate until prices normalize. Choice of (a) or (b) to be agreed in the SOW.
- Phased activation credits: 50% waived commitment for months 1–2 (to aid ramp) to reduce your initial risk.

I cc'ed Karthik, Naomi, and Ben for quick internal review on the guardrail wording and any finance approvals needed. I have a draft MAP and the capacity schedule attached (triton_capacity_map_v1.pdf, triton_capacity_schedule.xlsx). If you want I can convert the guardrail bullets into SOW language.

Next steps: internal alignment on the discount/credit mechanics; I will follow up once I have internal sign-off and send a short customer-ready proposal.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Account Exec, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-11T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Sizing & Reserved Capacity for TritonHealth pilot — pricing guardrails

Team —

Forwarding Anjali's ask + my draft bullets below. Need a fast path on approvals: Triton wants something customer-ready by 7/19 for Procurement. Specifics I need from you:

1) Karthik — is the proposed GPU-indexation trigger (12% q/q) acceptable to Sales Ops/Legal? If finance insists on a hard pass-through rather than credits, we need to know now.
2) Naomi — can Finance support a 60-day temporary credit mechanism if we see an exceptional GPU price spike? If yes, what guardrails (total $ cap /% of deal) do you need?
3) Ben — any operational constraints on phasing activation (20 -> 30 -> 40 -> burst 60)? Will we guarantee burst capacity or is that best-effort to avoid overpromising?

Quoted for context:
"High level: ... baseline discount band of 18% ... GPU-indexation fallback ... temporary credit ... phased activation credits: 50% waived commitment for months 1–2..."

Please reply with a one-liner approval/condition and I'll incorporate and send to the customer. Timebox: 48 hours.

Thanks,
Marcus
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-12T11:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Sizing & Reserved Capacity for TritonHealth pilot — pricing guardrails

Marcus —

Quick answers:
1) Index trigger: 12% q/q is reasonable as a trigger for review. Sales Ops prefers not to do full automatic pass-throughs. Proposed structure: 12% trigger -> 30-day pricing review window -> if validated, we offer either (A) a one-time credit equal to 50% of the incremental delta for up to 60 days (cap: 6% of annual contract value), or (B) allow temporary burst to hosted pool at committed per-unit rate for up to 45 days. Customer selects A or B in SOW. This keeps us from taking open-ended risk.
2) Finance (Naomi) — Naomi confirmed she can support a credit mechanism with the ACL above but wants a maximum cap and requires that credits are reconciled quarterly and routed through Finance (no unilateral Sales credit). She also requests a simple formula in the SOW: credit = min(0.5 * delta_unit_cost * units_affected, 0.06 * ACV).
3) Ops (Ben) — We can commit to phased activation schedule as long as the SOW includes an agreed-on activation calendar and notice windows (14 days for a phase-up). Burst to hosted pool is available but not SLA-backed; we should explicitly label burst as non-SLA best-effort. If the customer needs SLA-backed burst, we need exec approval and an associated uplift.

Approvals required: Finance (Naomi) sign-off + Revenue Ops (Ben) ack; if customer asks for SLA-backed burst or higher credit cap (>6% ACV) escalate to Sales leadership.

Related: HubSpot deal TR-4821 has the ACV and ARR assumptions — see link: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/4821. I put draft SOW clauses in Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1xTritonDrafts.

Karthik
Head of Sales Ops

Date: 2028-07-22T11:07:00-07:00
Subject: Proposal: phased reserved sizing + GPU-price guardrail (TritonHealth TR-4821)

Anjali / Raj —

Thanks for the patience while we aligned internally. Attached are two artifacts: a one-page Mutual Action Plan (triton_capacity_map_v1.pdf) and a phased activation schedule (triton_capacity_schedule.xlsx). Summary (customer-ready):

What we propose
- Reserved commitment: 12 months, baseline reserved pool equivalent to 40 vGPUs (A100-equivalent). Activation phased: 20 vGPUs months 1–3, +10 vGPUs month 4, +10 vGPUs month 7. Burst allowed to 60 vGPUs for spikes.
- Pricing: 18% discount on the committed tier for the 12-month term.
- Ramp support: 50% reduction in billed commitment for months 1–2 to reduce early-stage risk.

GPU-price guardrail (concise SOW clause to add)
- Trigger: If vendor GPU procurement unit cost increases by >12% quarter-over-quarter, Redwood will initiate a 30-day pricing review. The customer will choose one remedial action in the SOW: (A) a one-time credit equal to 50% of the verified incremental unit-cost delta for up to 60 days (credit cap = 6% of ACV), or (B) temporary allowed burst to Redwood hosted pool billed at the committed per-unit rate for up to 45 days. Credits will be reconciled quarterly.

Operational notes
- Burst to hosted pool is best-effort and not SLA-backed; if Triton needs SLA-backed burst, we can provide with an uplift (requires exec approval).
- Phase activation requires 14 days notice for each increase.

Next steps
1) If this structure looks acceptable, we will convert the bullets into SOW language and share a final MAP + SOW appendix for Procurement.
2) Please confirm choice between credit (A) or burst (B) for the remedial action and confirm the target activation dates for phases.

Attachments: triton_capacity_map_v1.pdf, triton_capacity_schedule.xlsx

Happy to hop on a short call if useful.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Account Exec, Enterprise
